body:
| | [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/wehEm_vu1NBVXOKYSqOxTOi34aJoCJC1EivM7Ih953zRu3g-wRB9ZrzqGpZimVkYVPaEH9LaYSOVWHiOlKjL9oCOmVvQ701OgwGK-s7iz_S5f9hCPmYYnDZi65Qjb3KZAGgo6pzAVRDLIMc9sLZ1Y2UyzdwjOO3OiFgCZNLaBRPk6PjvvRg5dKBReL28svZVHe5Tj7wrQBRqpspMopkkNpvG7qEJ12DPFVrggyr56_3P7UrVpoI9f9hF3CtXroE1mzKPVKZCxhL9lZugTOAg7FP9Vq4O6vhqQ9J7WQIAtVZH-YYeF_BGhmDIVvO9asdzRmNhgB5JIrnmRowd22eEZQ/3z7/TFNxRfF0QQq6aq8SjI7FTQ/h0/K0s-KX8tSDETliQXqtJlDBYsyLD_4ZrjAykDRsNGZHw)
---
Friend, At age 19 I walked into my Catholic college’s health clinic on Valentines Day. My period was late. The nurse walked into the exam room with my pregnancy test, congratulated me, and my stomach dropped to the floor. In shock, I walked out of the office and found my boyfriend. He could tell immediately that I had gotten news neither of us were ready to hear. I knew he wasn’t ready to be a father. I knew I was not ready to be a mother... I knew, deep down inside, that we did not stand a chance of raising a family together. I had a medical abortion at 6 weeks pregnant. I was confused when I was not depressed or sad afterwards, but relieved. My limited education of abortion had only given me the sense that all women who make this decision would be swallowed by regret for the rest of their lives. Up until this point I had identified as “Pro-life.” I grew up going to Catholic school and went to a Baptist church on weekends. But more than God or religion, what made me pro-life was my mother. My mother was a teen mom, and I had always told myself that If I ever found myself pregnant unexpectedly, I would do what my mother did. But my mother struggled. Young and with few resources, she had to work harder than _anyone_ I have ever known to support my brother and me. When I found out I was pregnant, the realities of my mother’s journey hit me square in the face. I was not ready to embark on that journey. I was in no place to provide for a child. My abortion experience changed me in a way I never saw coming, so much so that after I was recovered I interned at a Women’s health clinic in Atlanta that offered abortion services. In my role I would sit with women on the day of their abortion procedure. I helped them fill out their medical paperwork, I talked to them about the procedure, I offered them a compassionate ear, and I listened to their stories. I did this for two years. I have quite literally heard _hundreds_ of women’s stories on the day of their abortion procedure. That is why I am running for office; I know that when a woman walks into an abortion clinic, it is their saving grace. No one is there flippantly or gleefully. _**Women are there because they need to be.**_
---
| [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/wehEm_vu1NBVXOKYSqOxTOi34aJoCJC1EivM7Ih953zRu3g-wRB9ZrzqGpZimVkYWvsUOEEoY_sJEEryL6X44rXrSMH4toEysBiv-X3OBDAqxXeZJRVIVmj6hC2ztk-tf7y1QKhwBGRZf3A-dpGDEuvFNuYDYvzoSy4S4amG9Ezgn5pk3ufDdWLR7VvXARcCwezVzjkhY5hW95ggPUP2pH8PhFvx9OAhow_d_KYMInswX52wfLbBeBroeALpmmtTGR6-gZMQkLQLbgfiBUfkkuXuMKvLk3Hk_zEkssTO6eHnU0BPHY8vjgsNYEe8thx-Nn_uh4RYP8A0smpQnTDZF4u-z6CIc_RPbzqEaXC2jfGDqpfGPaP0iG80mWA1PkLm/3z7/TFNxRfF0QQq6aq8SjI7FTQ/h1/ko7qE3ws7XDLT3GvX1wq79qqZNlKWW1OGlkQRP2xqxE)
---
_Watch my first campaign video here._
---
A woman having an abortion is in a crisis. Whether the crisis is borne out of money, career, existing children, or tragically a violent conception or medical emergency, abortion is necessary healthcare. I have never been a fan of the term “choice.” People choose abortion like people choose car accidents. People can drive as safely as they can, and still, sometimes accidents happen. You can take any number of precautions in your life, but things will still happen that are out of your control. I am now a proud 35 year old single mother of a beautiful six year old daughter. I have just graduated from law school and work for a wonderful environmental non-profit. I have a children’s book coming out next year. And for the first time in my life, I do not have to work two jobs to make it and life is absolutely wonderful. _So why mess it up by running for office?_ Because if Louisiana’s current abortion laws had existed when I was 19, I would not have had the chance to build my life to a place where I was truly ready to provide for a child. The Louisiana State Legislature has [passed a law](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/P8Elou2Rvc0qoMPEUZrMXTEBokwJ0izHXMWrpJl2hHxMFYkKnUFaILCcOQyL90ZV-1t6Mt8I-8S8h5qcAg7GjNzSgyGMkdUfUlLhaMwJGJeDfWUDjkmNISJ2SYxOklYFMhCWIyV4GdQSluSyr4UaHWk8ohMQRHoXQzCerYzoZmAa6Xsm3yUx0Mxx0FuKVMMVZHM1z2nLNp9K2e1YSU5mYm94MP2DxFSGRtMhnRk7meYcBlXfwi_KdwTAccN3PG8igPBI4LuqG3HKZ66eKlqrywTCpMZ_5WOBxi4g6vu8WT96A-xLf7D_a0jH5UAVjnlc2t4PoMh7xHW7rwaG51sJpeV3nDaOrCNeXoXOUxS-LM0/3z7/TFNxRfF0QQq6aq8SjI7FTQ/h2/wviDq9aZTrS7iX2DMsz6BQZeAb475KcHh5heZdKt18U) stating that every woman who falls pregnant is forced to give birth. **Louisiana has the harshest abortion law in the country.** Too young or too old? Too bad. Too sick? Too bad. No partner? Too bad. Bad partner? Too bad. Financially struggling? Too bad. Rape? Too bad. Incest? Too bad. If anyone, doctor or otherwise, helps a woman have an abortion, they are liable to face up to 15 years in jail and 200k in civil penalties. **This is a disgrace to the women and families of Louisiana and we must dismantle Louisiana’s cruel abortion landscape before it is too late.**

clean_body: | | Friend, At age 19 I walked into my Catholic college’s health clinic on Valentines Day. My period was late. The nurse walked into the exam room with my pregnancy test, congratulated me, and my stomach dropped to the floor. In shock, I walked out of the office and found my boyfriend. He could tell immediately that I had gotten news neither of us were ready to hear. I knew he wasn’t ready to be a father. I knew I was not ready to be a mother... I knew, deep down inside, that we did not stand a chance of raising a family together. I had a medical abortion at 6 weeks pregnant. I was confused when I was not depressed or sad afterwards, but relieved. My limited education of abortion had only given me the sense that all women who make this decision would be swallowed by regret for the rest of their lives. Up until this point I had identified as “Pro-life.” I grew up going to Catholic school and went to a Baptist church on weekends. But more than God or religion, what made me pro-life was my mother. My mother was a teen mom, and I had always told myself that If I ever found myself pregnant unexpectedly, I would do what my mother did. But my mother struggled. Young and with few resources, she had to work harder than anyone I have ever known to support my brother and me. When I found out I was pregnant, the realities of my mother’s journey hit me square in the face. I was not ready to embark on that journey. I was in no place to provide for a child. My abortion experience changed me in a way I never saw coming, so much so that after I was recovered I interned at a Women’s health clinic in Atlanta that offered abortion services. In my role I would sit with women on the day of their abortion procedure. I helped them fill out their medical paperwork, I talked to them about the procedure, I offered them a compassionate ear, and I listened to their stories. I did this for two years. I have quite literally heard hundreds of women’s stories on the day of their abortion procedure. That is why I am running for office; I know that when a woman walks into an abortion clinic, it is their saving grace. No one is there flippantly or gleefully. Women are there because they need to be. | Watch my first campaign video here. A woman having an abortion is in a crisis. Whether the crisis is borne out of money, career, existing children, or tragically a violent conception or medical emergency, abortion is necessary healthcare. I have never been a fan of the term “choice.” People choose abortion like people choose car accidents. People can drive as safely as they can, and still, sometimes accidents happen. You can take any number of precautions in your life, but things will still happen that are out of your control. I am now a proud 35 year old single mother of a beautiful six year old daughter. I have just graduated from law school and work for a wonderful environmental non-profit. I have a children’s book coming out next year. And for the first time in my life, I do not have to work two jobs to make it and life is absolutely wonderful. So why mess it up by running for office? Because if Louisiana’s current abortion laws had existed when I was 19, I would not have had the chance to build my life to a place where I was truly ready to provide for a child. The Louisiana State Legislature has stating that every woman who falls pregnant is forced to give birth. Louisiana has the harshest abortion law in the country. Too young or too old? Too bad. Too sick? Too bad. No partner? Too bad. Bad partner? Too bad. Financially struggling? Too bad. Rape? Too bad. Incest? Too bad. If anyone, doctor or otherwise, helps a woman have an abortion, they are liable to face up to 15 years in jail and 200k in civil penalties. This is a disgrace to the women and families of Louisiana and we must dismantle Louisiana’s cruel abortion landscape before it is too late. | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: or Thank you for support at this critical stage of our campaign. Together we will make abortion legal again in Louisiana. Sincerely, Britt Gondolfi | To contribute via check, please address to: P.O. Box 2481, Hammond, LA 70404 britt@gondolfi.com | | Sent via . A proud son of Tennessee, Ryan's story is one of dedication, courage, and sacrifice. He gave it all in service to our great nation, tragically losing his life in the [gut-wrenching events near Kabul airport.](http://links.burchettforcongress.com/u/click?_t=feefb5ad83f24ba4b99ac997c1b47e86&_m=085233dad08a4731af19f28b08bcc7d2&_e=XQFjLuNfOUfYGy9zTC_2yvRGryl1hcd00E8J1cyLIrUpJeYRSB3FkaH6yMuSjNzNX90nseFj-MP63qKapwEnEU2WMU83BXF_j5KDBdwvh1ufASscz04G8SLTmVDpluVCGZm30cO60z0ZIfPbrKfGfam-LoZ6ZkzUWR5d5TJCG2vfuTSLWvs0bt6342PS8Ijpa4GFLdAYnACB-my9FZnJ7nx4TzaoyiTyeX61eADPZZtZIWNPJsVV4aQ9hnIigcxJE1qkyJfHxzc0JwPfE464i82ymKHPyUspZ42UAIC5oCo%3D) As we stood together last Saturday, we couldn't help but feel the weight of those 13 lives lost and the families forever changed. critical to safeguard and continue the fight for bodily autonomy, both locally,
nationally and globally.
This summer, Vice President Kamala Harris has been spending a lot of time
in Philadelphia because she knows the importance of Philadelphia’s electorate.
Our turnout is pivotal for this year’s crucial municipal elections and could
determine the outcome of next year’s Presidential race.
We must maintain the progress that has been made by the Biden-Harris
Administration - from holding the line to protect our Reproductive Rights to the
massive economic infusion of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and a swell in
manufacturing jobs, plus so much more. These programs have benefitted PA and
Philadelphia in important ways. Democrats deliver!
I intend to not only campaign for my own candidacy this year, but also for

name: John Fetterman
subject: I couldn’t be more thrilled
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Fetterman for PA
body:
If you know me, you know that for *many* years now I’ve supported legal weed.
#
Big news, Derek. **President Biden's administration is recommending that the DEA loosen marijuana restrictions + end its status as a Schedule I drug.**
If you know me, you know that for *many* years now I've supported legal weed. When President Biden was in Pittsburgh nearly a year ago, I used the opportunity to talk to him about the need to decriminalize marijuana. And now, with this massive win, we're making a big step forward. 💪💪💪
Moving weed from Schedule I will have huge benefits for people across PA + around the country. It will make it easier for folks like veterans who rely on it as a treatment for conditions like PTSD. And it will mean that stores in states that have decriminalized marijuana are able to more easily access bank services and funding that were difficult or impossible to get before.
But let's be clear: The science has always been on our side, but the DEA and its destructive “war on drugs” mindset has blocked reform. We have to keep up the pressure to take more action and pursue justice for those harmed by those policies.
With your support, I'll continue to be the LOUDEST (and tbh, probably the tallest) champion for legal weed + marijuana justice in the U.S. Senate.
**[Let's keep up our fight to legalize weed and end the racist War on Drugs — because it's working. If you're with me, chip in $5 or more to our people-powered campaign now.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20230831-1?refcode=em20230831-1-8538&refcode2=8538_434096_R4uLj5&akid=8538%2E434096%2ER4uLj5)**
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20230831-1?amount=5&refcode=em20230831-8538&refcode2=8538_434096_R4uLj5&akid=8538%2E434096%2ER4uLj5)**
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20230831-1?refcode=em20230831-1-8538&refcode2=8538_434096_R4uLj5&akid=8538%2E434096%2ER4uLj5)
To be clear, the last time I smoked weed in earnest was at Burning Man in 1999.
Thanks, Derek. I'm so proud of this team today.
❤️John
John Fetterman
U.S. Senator from Pennsylvania

| Meet **Mark Walker**

Congressman Mark Walker started his career in finance and, after earning his theology degree, Walker served 16 years as a pastor. In 2014, Walker stepped away from ministry and made a successful run for the U.S. Congress defeating a host of elected politicians. In 2015, Congressman Walker became the first member in an inaugural term to be elected Chair of the Republican Study Committee (RSC) - the largest caucus in Congress with 160 members and a position previously held by Vice President Pence and Congressman Jim Jordan.

In 2018, Walker was elected as Vice Chair of the entire conference, becoming the highest rated conservative to serve in the top four leadership positions in Congress. Walker is also the last member of Congress to secure a floor vote on a balanced budget amendment and led the House on HBCU initiatives winning the United Negro College Fund President’s list award. Congressman Walker served on multiple committees and in 2019, Walker was appointed to ranking member on the Committee on Homeland Security’s Intelligence and Counter-Terrorism’s subcommittee. Walker was co-chair of the bicameral prayer caucus for five years and also won the GOP MVP award as the starting pitcher on the Republican baseball team for the annual charity game.

Congressman Walker was redistricted out of his seat and stepped away from Congress in 2021. Walker ran for U.S. Senate in 2022 and was endorsed by Senators Tim Scott and James Lankford, Gov. Mike Huckabee, Hall of Fame Coach Tony Dungy and more than 200 pastors across North Carolina. Walker is currently the president of a political consulting business called Advancing Hope USA, and advocated for the two North Carolina Supreme Court candidates and 4 North Carolina Court of Appeals candidates through his independent expenditure organization, Win the Courts during this past general election. Congressman Walker and his wife Kelly, a Family Nurse Practitioner and flight trauma specialist, have been married for thirty years and have three children.

**You Loot, We Shoot** On the heels of an almost Cat 4 hurricane, Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis said he had**[directed law enforcement to "protect people's property.](https://caucusroom.cmail19.com/t/i-l-ayuddjd-trhiujldw-j/)"** **A School that Doesn't know History** A 12-year-old boy from Colorado was booted from class over a Gadsden flag patch on his backpack. **[You won't believe what the school said the flag represents!](https://caucusroom.cmail19.com/t/i-l-ayuddjd-trhiujldw-t/)** **There is no Climate Emergency** International scientists have **[jointly signed a declaration dismissing the existence of a climate crisis](https://caucusroom.cmail19.com/t/i-l-ayuddjd-trhiujldw-i/)** and insisting that carbon dioxide benefits Earth, contrary to the popular alarmist narrative. **Moderators Announced** Stuart Varney, Dana Perino, and UNIVISION's Ilia Calderon are set to co-moderate the second Republican primary debate.**[Will you watch this debate?](https://caucusroom.cmail19.com/t/i-l-ayuddjd-trhiujldw-d/)**

**Justice** District of Columbia has **[settled a class-action lawsuit filed by six gun owners](https://caucusroom.cmail19.com/t/i-l-ayuddjd-trhiujldw-h/)** who were arrested for violating gun control laws that the courts have since struck down. **Let****'s [have a good laugh](https://caucusroom.cmail19.com/t/i-l-ayuddjd-trhiujldw-k/)!**
* A fun little **[challenge](https://caucusroom.cmail19.com/t/i-l-ayuddjd-trhiujldw-u/).**
* I**[finally](https://caucusroom.cmail19.com/t/i-l-ayuddjd-trhiujldw-p/) **got it.
* He **[didn't know](https://caucusroom.cmail19.com/t/i-l-ayuddjd-trhiujldw-x/)**.

Going toe-to-toe with Lauren Boebert and Marjorie Taylor Greene on the Oversight Committee.

And, most bluntly of all, _**women candidates raise less money at every phase of an election cycle compared to men**_.

**That's where my friends at EMILYs List come in.** For 38 years and counting, EMILYs List has been raising money to elect Democratic pro-choice women up and down the ballot and across the nation. name: Elizabeth Warren
subject: re: The series finale of The Sopranos
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Warren for Senate
body:
The last time Congress increased the federal minimum wage was sixteen years ago.

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=34%2E4032634%2EZa0e2R)
---
The way I see it, no one in this country should work full-time and still live in poverty — period. But today’s federal minimum wage can’t keep a full-time working mama and her baby out of poverty. Not to mention, recent studies have found that a minimum wage earner working a 40-hour week can’t afford a two-bedroom apartment anywhere in the country. The last time Congress increased it was 2007. Sixteen years ago. Three presidencies ago. The first-ever iPhone was just announced for sale. The series finale of The Sopranos had just aired. Yeah, that long ago. That is wrong, and that is why I’m fighting to raise it. **So I’m co-sponsoring a bill with Senator Bernie Sanders and dozens of our colleagues to increase the minimum wage to $17 an hour.** [**It’s long past time to deliver a raise to tens of millions of hardworking Americans, and we need to mobilize as much support as possible to get momentum behind this bill. So add your name if you agree our government must raise the minimum wage, and let’s fight side by side to make it happen.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/wfs-raise-minimum-wage?source=EMZ16B_MIN_E_20230831_V1S1_AK_F10&t=8&akid=34%2E4032634%2EZa0e2R) | [**ADD MY NAME**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/wfs-raise-minimum-wage?source=EMZ16B_MIN_E_20230831_V1S1_AK_F10&t=9&akid=34%2E4032634%2EZa0e2R)
---
This is an issue that hits close to home for me.
After my daddy had a heart attack, he couldn’t work for a while. Bills piled up. We lost the family station wagon, and it looked like the house could be next.
But one day, I walked in on my mother pacing back and forth in her bedroom, with a black dress laid out on the bedspread. The dress that only came out for weddings, funerals, and graduations. “We are not going to lose this house,” she kept saying. “We are not going to lose this house.”
She’d never worked outside the home. She was terrified. But she knew what she had to do. She put on that dress, she walked down the street to Sears, and she got a minimum wage job that saved our house and saved our family.
But families in that same situation today wouldn’t be able to say the same thing. The cost of living has skyrocketed while wages have stayed stagnant. Greedy corporations are taking advantage of working families any chance they get. CEOs are being paid 399 times as much as a typical worker. (We’ve also got a bill to address this, the Tax Excessive CEO Pay Act, which would tax companies on the basis of their CEO-to-worker compensation ratio.)
**Raising the federal minimum wage is part of how we put our government on the side of working people — not just the rich and powerful.**
[**But to get this done, Washington needs to see the American people demanding action. Add your name if you support raising the minimum wage to $17 an hour.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/wfs-raise-minimum-wage?source=EMZ16B_MIN_E_20230831_V1S1_AK_F10&t=10&akid=34%2E4032634%2EZa0e2R)
Thanks for being a part of this,
Elizabeth

P.S. Do you have any feedback on this plan or for our campaign in general? [**Please share with me here. I appreciate hearing your thoughts.**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/signup/wfs-share-your-feedback/?source=EMZ16B_MIN_E_20230831_V1S1_AK_F10&t=11&akid=34%2E4032634%2EZa0e2R)

| Peter,
---
| | Our so-called leaders think they have gotten away with turning their backs on us.

As someone who's fed up with all the corruption and is running for Congress to unseat politicians who protect the status quo, I believe it's my duty to step up and demand some accountability.

Former Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich does too, and he’s urging Congress to hold Biden’s feet to the fire AND to also look into the corruption surrounding Barack Obama and Hillary Clinton. _I couldn’t agree more! _
---
| [ ](https://mcshanellc.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=ab8092551f57aee37054250c5&id=015f9ce661&e=54a81bd33c)
---
|
---
| Gingrich's words resonate deeply, especially as we learn about the thousands of incriminating emails connected to Biden's pseudonym accounts. The House GOP’s talk of an impeachment inquiry into Joe Biden is heating up.

But we can't stop there. We need to dig deeper and figure out what else has been going on, because it's way bigger than just Biden's son.

Fake names, secret servers – evidence of millions in pay-to-play schemes that enriched them while impoverishing us. **I'm sick of it, and I know you are too.** **I need to show that Nevadans are with me in my call to see that the Bidens, Obamas, Clintons in our government must ALL be held accountable for their deceit and lawlessness!**

**Peter, join me in taking a stand._We’re demanding that the same rule of law we are held to – is applied to them_!**

Friend, I dedicated my life to keeping our country safe as a U.S. Navy Officer.

# Party of the Constitution
---
Chairwoman Kristina Karamo held a press conference today at our Lansing headquarters to address the recent BOMBSHELL reports on election corruption from Muskegon.
In this conference, Kristina along with MIGOP State-Committee members Braden Giacobazzi, Lori Skibo, and Election Integrity Committee chair Phil O’Halloran asked why a voter registration company, who received millions of dollars from multiple Democratic Party Organizations including Joe Biden would need five handguns and five semiautomatic rifles, some with suppressors (the same weapons the Democratic Party says you shouldn’t have).

* Who were they prepared to shoot?
* What were they defending?

Friend, This summer, deadly heat waves have swept our nation, endangering millions struggling with unaffordable utility bills. **No one should have to go without water and other basic needs—especially not during this extreme heat.** Water, electricity, heating, cooling, and life-sustaining services are not commodities to be privatized or sold. These are basic human needs and rights, and they must be accessible to all. But across the country, for-profit utility companies continue to raise rates, cutting off essential services for families who cannot afford to pay. Along with my colleagues Cori Bush and Jamaal Bowman, I’ve led the fight in Congress to protect our human right to safe and reliable utilities such as water and electricity. **Now we’re demanding immediate legislative action to pause utility shutoffs during months of extreme heat, forgive utility debt accrued by low-wealth households, establish cooling centers and water facilities for people in need, and more.** [**Please sign if you agree: We must safeguard struggling families during this extreme heat.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/P8Elou2Rvc0qoMPEUZrMXcOpy_XqN4R2ZGjoK-5zZnl-vRswUTt0wSRsVUTolC16Mso0yxGx82R0cwdj4ag8Z-dsZs6Ymp4Kt_Moi5-KiMQercI8l-WwVA4NRHAgED89EntYEbWh3Tda4mZgQSKEhEzNsXdT2KbgioQvO1v026d5OxZt-CjE0tXujrwka_v9mjieBGFdVvbx8Vp0wkz9A78POSW479vWcNBQ9cp4HJaK05OeSxrcVSo7cU8HaHWNkErKiOH3gNbMIyzla49Yw6oDpD9bV_cjkHunwJG_PiaWJpMBYbqi-G6mJXVs4pfEviqwCw4CKApqvtW8dqvQcJYAbUTaDo7gaf2BT03ruSyU2TrRtlqnwycLQ8O6gWPIVJd_n_MKJU4-4OmeJSNcxQAC8hiIYOnftpZ7cX-7_YAZ9rl8B00ic11ECySiH80P6AMKor984D-mzmehZZBZQIRGTBtQUESqyrXLNbhyfwukjJsqiBhDhi_7Yf8O0TwOUTrFVSjSf4ts7qThEGunHno5dhJpemKWTcBrfGtYerWe9bGvm7qyRnbMxUxdKUFs/3z7/sCXxVbT_Tti95OUqLDRdlA/h1/oF0Kv4fJlDFHOwmR_Sy5V2zz7GE5xsz0jIW1g6U3l30) | [SIGN ON](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/P8Elou2Rvc0qoMPEUZrMXcOpy_XqN4R2ZGjoK-5zZnl-vRswUTt0wSRsVUTolC16Mso0yxGx82R0cwdj4ag8Z-dsZs6Ymp4Kt_Moi5-KiMQercI8l-WwVA4NRHAgED89EntYEbWh3Tda4mZgQSKEhISh1O8oajx3pglIWl8DHi-S9Ydpj6bQVzriLnlfUkPsBCMq65vMsYbNpqMtiwh4AKiHlXAvvliYEQP7xo71OjQL1vQwMGOunlvI7aIDRpRIwsVPd1ZAUDYnHwAZjo_TM4kc7jLuVXl7YKliJGgyA4JSEJxWWxeyz5P0bs0IMCzKQSW9X_9F8yCIhgK3HZjLJ5pbzMt9JwKc_cyoCzwzXUd_m-wSOEBrC4EXCylO6aWEBNyHJIr-U0b3Da0j_G9Bh-a6JDQgyR3IvrN7ia0w1r3hy__-RudgFR-5iVMQcEoGD3XlPR0QBu9_Yi_K8voX8W-riG_whoqpvOFrMWYgtc-9YWPqchEKEZVmX_C1pXBSG0NewsjtoAukQGHgiGp2q-lpsvOJLTr3Q5UA8mLBe7bcXru46VfQrdZ7cjMuRdEN/3z7/sCXxVbT_Tti95OUqLDRdlA/h2/azKSMsq05TxPfhqT0I-R899DecXKvypP_R3KhLySGmc)

With most U.S. residents living paycheck to paycheck, millions of families cannot afford the skyrocketing prices of these essential services.
**For years, as a community activist and in Congress, I’ve fought for the human right to clean and safe drinking water** , including by securing more than $1.1 billion in federal funding to assist low-income households who need support in paying off their water bills and paying for fees to reconnect their water services.
We passed legislation through the House of Representatives to stop water and power shutoffs during the pandemic, require reconnection of services, and aid families suffering due to limited water access.
**Now I’m joining with Cori Bush and Jamaal Bowman to call on Congress to implement urgent and necessary short-term solutions like a moratorium on utility shutoffs, and then to address the systemic causes of utility injustice and climate chaos.**
We need bolder action from our federal government, including phasing out fossil fuels, banning utility shutoffs permanently, and funding renewable energy and publicly owned drinking water systems.
We know that climate change intensifies events like storms and heat waves. But many utilities are failing to make critical infrastructure updates for climate resilience, especially in Black and brown communities—leading to long, frequent, and deadly power outages, including in my community.

body:

My least favorite part about campaigning for Congress is fundraising.

_Shocker, I know..._

Regardless of how I feel about it, the reality is that ever since the _Citizens United_ decision, elections have become more expensive, and candidate fundraising has become much more vital.

Midnight tonight marks an important fundraising deadline, and I'm not exaggerating when I say that how we do will impact how strong of a campaign we can run. The great news is that we've seen a ton of contributions coming in. Yours would go a long way in helping us meet the mark!

**Can you use the personalized link below to chip in $3 before midnight?**
**[https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lf-q3-2023?refcode=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/69020561/424829691/-1241314520?refcode=em-8.31.23-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM1MzYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiODQ5YzczOTAtNTE0OC1lZTExLWEzZjEtMDAyMjQ4MzJlYjczIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=JC9m6ViWnQIuPXegjalbHynjkQ4oqKtYx5f8MFc7_u0=)**

Believe it or not, a significant chunk of our donations are generated by emails like this one. We don't have billionaires or big special interests backing us the way others in this race might. Everything is at stake in 2024, from voting rights to access to reproductive health care to protecting our state’s natural resources.
National Republicans have put Michigan at the top of their target list. We're rounding up our best supporters to fight back so we can keep making progress on these issues (and more) facing our state.

# [](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/35?t=1&akid=500%2E791427%2E_ZO024)

Friends - We’ll keep this quick.
This is our final request before tonight’s fundraising deadline. We’re so close to our goal, and your donation could push us over the top.
Reaching this goal is critical because we know that Ilhan’s opponent will be well-funded by special interests and backed by the same super PACs that spent big against us last year.
**[Can you make a $3 donation to our campaign to send Ilhan Omar back to Congress in 2024? We cannot fall short of our goal now.](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-aug23.SAeyb4&refcode=em230831-2-t2&t=2&akid=500%2E791427%2E_ZO024)**
_AUGUST FUNDRAISING DEADLINE_
**EMAIL:** dpwillis67@gmail.com
**DEADLINE:** Midnight
**REMAINDER TO GOAL:** $3,792
**SUGGESTED DONATION** : $3
Most campaigns in our situation right now might just call up a corporate PAC, ask them to max out with a $5,000 check, and call it a night.
But that’s now how this movement works. We fund this campaign the right way — from working people donating what they can, when they can, and we’re proud of that.
Thank you for being part of this!
Team Ilhan
**[CONTRIBUTE](https://act.ilhanomar.com/go/7?c0=io-em-aug23.SAeyb4&refcode=em230831-2-t2&t=3&akid=500%2E791427%2E_ZO024)**

PAID FOR BY ILHAN FOR CONGRESS
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is a very important way we communicate with supporters like you, but if you want to, you can **[unsubscribe here](https://act.ilhanomar.com/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?source=em-footer&t=4&akid=500%2E791427%2E_ZO024)**. You can also **[sign up to receive fewer emails](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/fewer-emails/?source=em-footer&t=5&akid=500%2E791427%2E_ZO024)**.
Submit this form to [**update your contact information**](https://act.ilhanomar.com/signup/update-contact-info/source=em-footer?t=6&akid=500%2E791427%2E_ZO024)
Ilhan is counting on our people-powered grassroots movement to fund this campaign. If you can, stand with us by **[making a contribution today](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/io-em-footer/?refcode=em-footer&t=7&refcode2=500_791427__ZO024&akid=500%2E791427%2E_ZO024)**.
Ilhan for Congress
PO Box 33079
Washington D.C., 20033

subject: Rallying our people-power
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
The only way our movement can be prepared to fight for our future is by ensuring we have the tools and resources to keep up our momentum.
#
Today is the final day of August — and the final day of our push to raise $350,000 before midnight tonight.
**Take a look at our progress so far:**
As a grassroots movement, we need to use our collective people-power to support Alexandria and continue fighting for our progressive vision of change. [In these final hours, will you make a donation of any amount to help us close the gap on our goal before midnight tonight?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20230831-pm.Qiu0rD&refcode=em20230831-4911-P_FND_EGR_GFM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=4911%2E2526796%2Eg1LNL-)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20230831-pm.Qiu0rD&refcode=em20230831-4911-P_FND_EGR_GFM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=20&akid=4911%2E2526796%2Eg1LNL-)**
Not only do we need to be prepared to support Alexandria against her MAGA Republican opposition — we need to rally to protect our hard-fought progress from an entire movement that wants to do away with our efforts. We won’t let them win.
The only way our movement can be prepared to fight for our future is by ensuring we have the tools and resources to keep up our momentum. And remember, Alexandria doesn’t do a minute of call time asking donors for big checks. We’re relying on this movement to reach our fundraising goals.
That’s why we’re reaching out to our most dedicated supporters to ask one favor: [Can we count on you to rush a donation of any amount to ensure that we can keep pace with our plans to protect Alexandria, grow our momentum, and continue fighting for our progressive values?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20230831-pm.Qiu0rD&refcode=em20230831-4911-P_FND_EGR_GFM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=21&akid=4911%2E2526796%2Eg1LNL-)
Thank you for your continued support and faith in this movement. We couldn’t do this without you.
Pa’lante,
Team AOC

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/aoc-email-20230831-pm?refcode=em20230831-4911-P_FND_EGR_GFM&t=22&refcode2=4911_2526796_g1LNL-&akid=4911%2E2526796%2Eg1LNL-)** | **[Merch](https://shop.ocasiocortez.com/?utm_source=em-footer-20230831-4911-P_FND_EGR_GFM&t=23&akid=4911%2E2526796%2Eg1LNL-)**

**In the wake of the _Dobbs_ decision overturning _Roe v. Wade_ , we've turned our outrage into a surge of grassroots energy similar to that of 1992**, which was named the "Year of the Woman" after EMILYs List membership grew exponentially and we elected four new women to the Senate and 20 to the House.

This cycle, we're fighting hard to elect more Democratic pro-choice women up and down the ballot and restore abortion access across the country. If we miss our End-of-Month goal, we won't have enough resources to keep up this critical work. **So, please, we're asking one final time: can you take a moment to read Ellen's message and donate toward our $150,000 End-of-Month goal before midnight tonight?

[https://emilyslist.org/go/End-August-Strong](https://click.everyaction.com/k/69022539/424837005/1205285870?sourceid=1051848&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMGNhYjcyMi01ODQ4LWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=J5C__m1UwgMOys4eZy3RbvNFpuACHZpVJXFHy9U4fF0=&emci=a484bf1c-5848-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&emdi=d0cab722-5848-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&ceid=5177934)** Thank you,

the EMILYs List team _\----------Original Message---------
From: Ellen R. Malcolm
Sent: Mon., Aug. 28, 2023_ [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/69022540/424837006/1205285870?sourceid=1051848&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMGNhYjcyMi01ODQ4LWVlMTEtYTNmMS0wMDIyNDgzMmViNzMiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=J5C__m1UwgMOys4eZy3RbvNFpuACHZpVJXFHy9U4fF0=&emci=a484bf1c-5848-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&emdi=d0cab722-5848-ee11-a3f1-00224832eb73&ceid=5177934) Peter,

It's clear as day that Democrats are more fired up than ever to elect pro-choice women.

We've seen Democratic pro-choice women defeat Republicans nationwide; anti-choice ballot initiatives have been overwhelmingly rejected by voters in not-so-blue states like Kansas and Ohio; Wisconsin elected pro-choice champion **Janet Protasiewicz** to their state Supreme Court (with EMILYs List's support!); and state leaders are fighting hard to pass pro-choice ballot measures.

**I've seen this kind of grassroots energy before — back in 1992**. That was the year EMILYs List grew our membership by 600%, elected four new women to the Senate, and elected _20_ to the House. It quickly became known as the "Year of the Woman."
